html:
The "royal road of the interior land", a trade route of about 2,560 kilometres from Mexico City north to the Spanish colony of New Mexico, used from 1598 to 1882. It was the longest of the royal roads of New Spain.

Its southern part was a silver route, running through mining towns such as Zacatecas. In 1598 Juan de Oñate led settlers north along it to found New Mexico among the Pueblo peoples, and the road was extended to Santa Fe. Large wagon trains made the trip only every few years at first, taking months. They carried tools, cloth, church goods and settlers north, and brought back hides, wool, salt and piñon nuts, as well as Indigenous captives sold as servants.

The road was the lifeline of New Mexico, and the route of the Spanish return after the Pueblo Revolt. After Mexican independence it linked with the Santa Fe Trail to the United States. The railway replaced it in the 1880s.
